newsitem.title: USA: KeyCorp Q3 expenses up, sees decline in Q4.
newsitem.headline: KeyCorp Q3 expenses up, sees decline in Q4.

text.p: KeyCorp said Thursday it expects fourth quarter non-interest expense to be "appreciably lower" than in the third quarter.
KeyCorp said expenses increased seven percent in the third quarter from a year earlier.
The company is working to improve the expense efficiency ratio, with a target of 55 percent by the end of next year, it said.
The company said expenses were higher in the third quarter due to acquisitions and increases in personnel and marketing spending.

In order to reach its target of a 55 percent efficiency ratio by "around the end of next year," KeyCorp said it had "initiated a comprehensive review of (its) branch delivery system and overall cost structure."
KeyCorp reported third quarter non-interest expense of $615 million, up $54 million, or 10 percent, from the year-ago quarter.

Excluding the impact of a one-time Savings Association Insurance Fund assessment, non-interest expense was up $37 million, or seven percent, reflecting a $22 million increase in personnel expense and an $11 million increase in marketing expense.
